newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade very slow - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade very slow - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets at midday on Monday were slow, with not enough sales to test the market, feedlot sources said.
Early bids at $66.00 to $67.00 were steady to $1.00 lower than last sales Friday at $67.00. The bids were generally passed by owners asking mostly $68.00, with a few at $69.00, they said.
About 400 head of steers and heifers sold at $67.00 per cwt in Kansas, sources there said.
Showlists were expected steady to slightly larger amid projections for a carryover from last week of mostly unfinished cattle, cattle feeders said.

Fed cattle activity this week was expected to be light going into the upcoming Memorial Day holiday weekend, they said. The beef market also was seen thin, particularly following last week's hefty sales, with most retailers finished booking orders for the holiday and end-of-month advertising features, sources said.

Last week's fabricated beef sales of 1,492 loads was the third largest of the year behind 1,629 the week ended April 11 and 1,735 the week ended March 14, USDA statistics showed. Beef prices at midday Monday were quoted up $0.83 to down $0.02 per cwt on 69 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
